name: Hungary
summary_text: Hungary is in a fast-improving post-Orbán transition. The most acute traveler-facing risk — the 2025 Pride ban with facial-recognition identification of attendees — has stopped: the 2026 Budapest Pride was held freely. Péter Magyar's Tisza party won a supermajority in April 2026, ending 16 years of Orbán rule, and the EU's top court has ruled that Hungary's 2021 "child protection" law breaches EU values (handing the new government a repeal mandate). However, the Orbán-era laws remain on the books: a total ban on domestic legal gender recognition (2020), the "child protection" content law, and a constitutional amendment banning LGBTQ public events. The structural weakness that has not changed with the election is detention: a German court in 2025 blocked the extradition of a non-binary person to Hungary because of prison conditions and the person's identity, and watchdogs report transphobia in prisons with a "culture of silence." Bathrooms are unrestricted, there is no criminalisation of trans identity, and the Schengen border poses no trans-specific entry friction. Social hostility lingers outside Budapest, but the state-led demonization that characterised the Orbán years has ended.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying France24 piece (June 2026) covers LGBTQ rights in Hungary after the election - 'we are very hopeful that changes will be made'.

AP (Jun 2026): 'Hungary holds its first Budapest Pride in the post-Orbán era' — tens of thousands march in the 31st Budapest Pride, the first since Viktor Orbán was voted out, against the backdrop of his era's anti-LGBT laws.

The Dissident analysis (April 2026) by Alejandra Caraballo: what Hungary's election (Tisza's 138 seats, ending Orbán's rule) actually means for LGBTQ people - a return to democratic baseline, not liberation. Details the 'constitutional architecture of erasure': the May 2020 total ban on legal gender recognition (redefining 'nem' as immutable biological sex), forcing trans Hungarians to carry mismatched documents.

Wikipedia overview: same-sex activity legal since 1961; legal gender change de facto impossible since 2018 and explicitly illegal since 2020; the 2021 child-protection law restricts 'promotion' of homosexuality/gender change; the 2025 Pride ban; discrimination protections and public opinion.

sources.title: Unprecedented ruling finds Hungary's anti-LGBTQ laws in breach of EU values
sources.claim_summary: BBC (April 2026): the European Court of Justice ruled Hungary's anti-LGBTQ laws (2021 'child protection' ban on 'promotion' of homosexuality or gender change to under-18s) violate EU rules and - unprecedentedly - the founding values of Article 2 of the EU Treaty; the law stigmatised trans and non-heterosexual people by associating them with paedophilia. Ruling came nine days after Hungarians voted to end Orbán's rule.

sources.title: Budapest Pride: “Anti-queer laws can be repealed with two-third majority” | Niha+
sources.claim_summary: niHaplus (April 2026): Budapest Pride spokesperson Johanna Majercsik says anti-queer laws can be repealed with a two-thirds majority; Tisza's 138 seats give it that power, but its silence on LGBTQ+ rights raises questions; the most urgent issue is restoring the right of assembly (2025 Pride ban). Recaps the 2012 two-sex constitutional amendment, 2020 adoption ban, and the 2021 Child Protection Act conflating LGBTQ+ people with child abusers.

Hungarian Helsinki Committee / Háttér Society national report (2025) on LGBTIQ detainees in Hungary, part of the EU-funded 'Strengthening the rights of LGBTIQ detainees in the EU' project - the situation and rights of LGBTIQ people in Hungarian detention amid the current legal and political climate.

sources.title: World Report 2025: Hungary | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW World Report 2025 Hungary chapter: the government's assault on rule of law continued in 2024, including a law giving a government-appointed body broad powers to harass civil society and independent media; includes a Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity section.

sources.title: 62023CJ0247
sources.claim_summary: ECJ judgment C-247/23 Deldits (13 March 2025): on GDPR accuracy and rectification of gender-identity data in Hungarian public registers - the Court addressed Hungary's administrative practice of demanding proof of gender-reassignment surgery before correcting data that was incorrect from the time of inclusion.

sources.title: The Coronavirus 2020: Hungary Is Using The COVID-19 Pandemic To Attack Transgender People
sources.claim_summary: BuzzFeed News (April 2020) by Patrick Strudwick: Hungary's new law will end legal gender recognition - 'It's just horrible,' a trans woman told BuzzFeed News; 'I don't want to lose good people because of this' - trans Hungarians speak out as the decree banning gender changes was published.
